info.bio:
Sandy Nelson's song "Teen Beat" rose to #4 on the charts in 1959. Subsequently he signed with the Imperial label and pounded out two more Top 40 hits, "Let There Be Drums", which went to #3 in Britain, and "Drums Are My Beat". All three were instrumentals (a feat seldom, if ever, repeated).

Sander L Nelson was born on 1 December 1938 in Santa Monica, California. He attended high school with Jan Berry, Dean Torrence (who together became Jan and Dean), and Kim Fowley.

scenes.name: Antes del diluvio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La «edad oscura» del rock'n'roll: los rebeldes son sustituidos por ídolos adolescentes educados y el Brill Building devuelve el poder a los compositores profesionales. Pero en esos años se incuban la revolución futura: la guitarra fuzz de Link Wray, los bailes de moda (el twist), el rock instrumental de guitarras (Duane Eddy, Ventures, Shadows), el calipso y el primer ska, el doo-wop más inventivo (Coasters, Drifters, Five Royales), el nacimiento del soul (Sam Cooke, Ray Charles, Motown, Stax), el estudio como instrumento de Joe Meek y el surf de los Beach Boys y del «muro de sonido» de Phil Spector.

podcast.title: Accused of Credit Theft
podcast.body: Richie Polador accused Sandy Nelson, along with Bruce Johnston and Kim Fowley, of having "no scruples whatsoever" and taking credit for songs like "Geronimo" and "Charge" that Polador claimed he wrote and recorded in his own studio. "There are three guys in the business who really have no scruples whatsoever. They are Bruce Johnston, Kim Fowley and Sandy Nelson, and I was Mr Scruples."

podcast.title: Sacked from The Debarrens
podcast.body: Sandy Nelson was fired from The Debarrens by Jan Berry for playing his drums too loudly. Upon his departure, he famously declared, "you'll see, I'm going to have a hit record that's only drums." This prophecy was later partially fulfilled with his hit "Team Beat." "In Sandy Nelson's case, he was sacked by Berry for playing his drum so loud."

podcast.title: Session Work Success
podcast.body: Nelson's departure from The Flips coincided with a significant increase in session work, as many people had seen him play live. His drum performance on The Teddy Bears' number one hit "To Know Him Is To Love Him," despite being described as rudimentary, significantly boosted his "cachet" for future gigs, including playing on Gene Vincent's "Crazy Times" LP. "Nelson's departure from the group coincided with him starting to get a great deal of session work from people who had seen him play live."
